svg.title: Figure 10.1 · Incident response flow with decision points
svg.desc: A ten-stage incident lifecycle running top to bottom. After an incident is detected, it is received, then triaged with a provisional severity. A severity decision point splits into a standard timeline and an emergency or critical timeline, which rejoin at stage 3. Stages 3 to 10 are protect and contain, assess, notify, correct and remedy, recover, verify and monitor, root cause analysis and review, and closure. The correct and remedy stage applies to predictive, generative and agentic incidents, with extra agentic checks noted on it. A dashed feedback loop sends new evidence back to severity, containment, scope and legal assessment, and communication.
svg.text: Figure 10.1 · Incident response flow with decision points
Preserve the evidence before anything changes it
Name an incident commander and set a provisional severity
Tier response time and update rhythm.
Act at once under a named authority.
Protect people and stop active harm
Then contain the system, data, access and supplier path
Scope, active cause, who is affected, legal duties, communication needs
Notify, each party on its own clock
Correct or eradicate the cause; remedy prior effects
Lookback and remedy applies to every system class:
Agentic extra checks: tool actions, transactions, commitments,
messages, state changes and downstream automations
Validated system, restricted service, or manual fallback
Verify recovery and watch for recurrence
Update severity and scope as the evidence changes
Root cause analysis and post-incident review
Sections 10.5 and 10.6; communication and documentation continue
Close only with evidence and owners
Technical, human, legal and process actions each covered
it does not only flow forward
Heavy outline: emergency branch and closure. Dashed lines: feedback. Stopping harm is not the same as remedying harm already done.
